issues.body:
Minted existentials change shape from `__sk1_e` to `__sk0_1_e`. `crates/sparq-reason/tests/n3_collect_stratified.rs:258-271` (`stratified_carried_existential_survives_a_colliding_source_label`) hard-codes the OLD shape: its stratum-2 source is `_:__st0___sk1_e`, chosen because that was exactly the label a FIXED `__st0_` carry rename would have produced for stratum 1's minted `_:e`. After this PR the carried label is `__st1___sk0_1_e`, so the source label no longer names the collision and the test passes for the wrong reason.

Proved empirically in an out-of-tree copy: with `fresh_carry_prefix` pinned to a constant `"__st0_"` (the bug the test exists to catch), `stratified_carried_blank_survives_a_colliding_source_label` FAILS (still has teeth) while `stratified_carried_existential_survives_a_colliding_source_label` PASSES. Its comment ("`_:e` skolemized to `__sk1_e`") is now false, so the next reader is also misled.

Secondary: the minted-label shape is user-visible in closure output and no CHANGELOG entry accompanies it.
issues.fix_hint: Update the stratum-2 source in that test to the label a fixed rename would now produce — `_:__st0___sk0_1_e` — and correct the comment to say `__sk0_1_e`. Verified out-of-tree: with that label the test PASSES at PR head and FAILS under a pinned `__st0_` carry rename, i.e. its teeth are restored. Better still, make it shape-independent (assert against the label actually observed in stratum 1's output) so the next mint-format change cannot defang it silently.
issues.title: Label-format change silently makes the existing stratified-existential regression test vacuous

issues.body:
`fresh_blank_prefix` (mod.rs:358-367) scans the whole label set per candidate `k` (`seen.iter().any(|l| l.starts_with(&prefix))`). A document whose blank labels are `__sk0_x .. __skN_x` forces N iterations over an N-element set — O(n^2). Before this PR that loop ran only in `reason_n3_stratified`'s carry path; line 479 now puts it on the default path of EVERY `run_closure`, i.e. every `reason_n3` call (sparq-py lib.rs:337/550, sparq-cli, the solid WAC/ACP paths) and every nested `formula_closure` run (mod.rs:1917), which is re-entered per binding per fixpoint round.

Measured out-of-tree (release, work box — NON-CANONICAL, order-of-magnitude only), adversarial `_:__sk{i}_x` fillers vs a benign `_:zz{i}_x` control:
  n= 2000: 13.6ms vs 6.7ms
  n= 4000: 38.7ms vs 11.2ms
  n= 8000: 136ms  vs 25.6ms
  n=16000: 511ms  vs 63.1ms
The adversarial-minus-control delta quadruples per doubling (6.8 / 27.5 / 110 / 448 ms) — clean quadratic attributable to this scan. Extrapolated, a ~160k-label document costs ~45s of pure prefix scanning on document content the caller does not control.
issues.fix_hint: Make it one pass instead of a rescan per k: iterate `seen` once, and for each label that starts with `family`, parse the digits up to the next `_` and insert that number into a `FxHashSet<usize>`/bitset of taken indices; then return the smallest absent index. That is O(n) total and preserves the exact current contract (`no existing label starts with family{k}_`). Apply it to `fresh_carry_prefix` too, since it shares the helper.
issues.title: fresh_blank_prefix is O(k*n) and now runs on every run_closure — quadratic on attacker-shaped documents

issues.body:
`sk_prefix` is computed once at entry (mod.rs:479) from `parsed`. Blank labels can still enter the fact set AFTER that point — e.g. a `log:semantics` / `log:parsedAsN3` result formula whose blanks are bound out through a variable (`{ ?d log:semantics ?f . ?f log:includes { ?x a :Foo } } => { ?x a :Bar }`) carries the EXTERNAL document's labels verbatim into the outer store. If that external document is itself a serialized closure containing `_:__sk0_1_e`, the outer run can mint the identical label and conflate the two nodes — the same capture this PR fixes, one level out. The same gap exists between an outer run and a nested `formula_closure` run, since each computes its prefix only over its own document.

I did not construct a triggering end-to-end counterexample, and this is pre-existing (the old fixed `__sk{n}_` scheme had it too), so I am reporting it as a residual, not as a regression from this PR. The in-code comment at mod.rs:476-478 is accurate as scoped ("every SOURCE blank label"); the concern is only that the class is not fully closed.
issues.fix_hint: Either rename ingested external/nested blanks apart on entry (the same trick `stratum_blanks` already uses at the stratum boundary), or state the residual explicitly in the comment at mod.rs:476-478 — e.g. 'fresh against the parsed source; labels ingested mid-run via log:semantics/parsedAsN3 are out of scope' — and file a bead for the ingest-side rename so the gap is tracked rather than implied closed.
issues.title: Freshness is proven only against the INITIAL parsed document, not labels ingested mid-run

issues.body:
1. `forward_rule_existential_avoids_source_blank_label_collision` asserts only `source_node != parent_node`. It would not catch a regression where the minted node is distinct from the source node but is NOT the node bound as the `:hasParent` object (i.e. the two conclusion triples stop co-referring) — the co-reference property is what makes per-firing skolemization meaningful.

2. `fresh_blank_prefix`'s doc (mod.rs:357) says 'absent from all existing labels', but the implemented predicate is stronger: no existing label may START WITH the prefix. That distinction is exactly what makes the namespace disjoint, so it is worth stating.
issues.fix_hint: Add `assert_eq!(parent_node, <object of the :hasParent triple>)` to pin co-reference between the two minted conclusion triples, and reword the `fresh_blank_prefix` doc to 'The smallest numbered `family{k}_` prefix that no existing label starts with.'
issues.title: New test asserts only distinctness; helper doc under-states the predicate

verdict.summary: The core fix is correct and the new test is genuinely non-vacuous: I copied the tree to /tmp, reverted the mint to the old `format!("__sk{sk_counter}_{l}")`, and `forward_rule_existential_avoids_source_blank_label_collision` went RED with `left: 3 right: 3` — the exact conflation. `document_blank_labels` covers every nested Term variant (Iri/Lit/Blank/Var/Formula/List/Triple — model.rs:8-25) plus backward rules, the parser keeps `_:label` verbatim (parser.rs:689) and `intern_blank` is label-keyed (mod.rs:3158), so the minted namespace `__sk{k}_` really is disjoint from source labels. The `__st`/`__sk` family split keeps the stratified carry rename sound. Two problems block approval. (1) Changing the minted label from `__sk1_e` to `__sk0_1_e` silently DEFANGS an existing regression test that hard-codes the old shape (tests/n3_collect_stratified.rs:258-271); I proved it vacuous by pinning `fresh_carry_prefix` to a fixed `__st0_` — the sibling test fails, that one now PASSES, i.e. it no longer catches the bug it pins, and its comment is now factually wrong. (2) `fresh_blank_prefix` is O(k*n) and now runs on EVERY `run_closure` (previously only the stratified carry path), giving measured quadratic blow-up on attacker-shaped input. Both are small, mechanical fixes.
